newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland frees money market fund investment - finmin.
newsitem.headline: Finland frees money market fund investment - finmin.

text.p: Finland will expand money market funds' chances to operate by letting them invest all capital in any money market paper, such as bank certificates, not just treasury bills, the finance ministry said on Monday.
It said it had confirmed new rules to the effect for Alfred Berg's Alred Berg Markka Rahamarkkinarahasto fund, which would take effect on August 1.
Bank certificates are currently the most liquid money market paper and provide the basis for the Bank of Finland's official Helibor rates.
"The decision confirms a fund company's right to invest all the mutual fund's assets in papers traded on the money market," the finance ministry said in a statement.
It said the decision was expected to "expand money market funds' chances to operate in Finland" and that the money market funds' total value was about seven billion markka.

Bank of Finland statistics show that the stock of bank certificates at end-1996 was 91.0 billion markka including central bank deposits, while the stock of outstanding government treasury bills was 40 billion.
